script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

---

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A warm, cozy living room, dimly lit by the glow of a fireplace. A pile of books on the coffee table, a record player in the corner, and the scent of freshly baked bread wafting through the air.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(whispering)
Welcome to Harmony Grove.

Enter MRS. JENKINS, a kind-faced, middle-aged woman wearing a cardigan and glasses, her hair pulled back into a neat bun. She sets down a plate of bread and a cup of tea on the coffee table.

MRS. JENKINS
(softly)
Ah, nothing quite like the peace and quiet of our little town. Come, take a seat.

Suddenly, the door creaks open and in walks MR. RIDLEY, a tall, handsome man in his late 30s, wearing a weathered leather jacket.

MR. RIDLEY
(roughly)
Mrs. Jenkins. I need your help.

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
Come, sit down. Tell me what's troubling you, Mr. Ridley.

---

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The town's quaint coffee shop, filled with the hum of conversation and the clinking of cups. A group of locals sit at a table, chatting and laughing.

Enter MRS. JENKINS and MR. RIDLEY.

MRS. JENKINS
(to the group)
Good morning, everyone. I have a new patient for you all to meet. This is Mr. Ridley.

The group turns to greet MR. RIDLEY with friendly smiles.

MR. RIDLEY
(awkwardly)
Hello. I've been meaning to come in for a while now. I've been having...troubles.

INT. MR. RIDLEY'S HOUSE - NIGHT

MR. RIDLEY's living room, cluttered with papers and magazines. He paces restlessly, muttering to himself.

MR. RIDLEY
(to himself)
I can't do this anymore. I can't keep living like this.

He reaches for the phone and dials a number.

---

INT. MRS. JENKINS' OFFICE - DAY

MRS. JENKINS sits behind her desk, listening intently as MR. RIDLEY pours out his story.

MR. RIDLEY
I've been hearing voices. They're getting louder and more insistent every day. I can't focus on anything else.

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
Mr. Ridley, I believe you. But you're not alone. I can help you through this.

---

EXT. TOWN PARK - DAY

MR. RIDLEY and MRS. JENKINS sit on a bench in the town park, surrounded by the sound of birds chirping and children playing.

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
You see, Mr. Ridley, our minds are like gardens. Sometimes, weeds grow. But with care and attention, we can weed them out and nurture the healthy growth.

MR. RIDLEY
(quietly)
I want to believe you. But the voices are so loud.

MRS. JENKINS
I know it's hard. But trust me, Mr. Ridley. Together, we can help you get through this.

---

INT. MR. RIDLEY'S HOUSE - NIGHT

MR. RIDLEY sits in his living room, surrounded by stacks of books and notebooks. He reads, writes, and takes deep breaths, trying to quiet the voices in his head.

MR. RIDLEY
(whispering to himself)
I can do this. I can silence the voices.

---

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

The town square, bustling with activity. MR. RIDLEY stands in the center, surrounded by the sounds of laughter and conversation. He closes his eyes and takes a deep breath.

MR. RIDLEY
(whispering)
I am stronger than the voices. I am in control.

---

INT. MRS. JENKINS' OFFICE - WEEKS LATER

Mrs. Jenkins looks up as MR. RIDLEY enters, a smile on his face.

MR. RIDLEY
Mrs. Jenkins, I haven't heard the voices in weeks. I'm feeling better than I have in a long time.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling back)
I'm so glad to hear that, Mr. Ridley. You've made great progress.

MR. RIDLEY
(gratefully)
Thank you, Mrs. Jenkins. I couldn't have done it without you.

---

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Jenkins sits in her warm, cozy living room, looking out the window at the peaceful town.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
And so, another soul has found peace in Harmony Grove.

---

FADE OUT.
